text:
Christopher Columbus

In the dim light of the hidden chamber, Frederick’s hand hovered over the crumbling parchment. The runes seemed to pulse with a malevolent energy, whispering promises of endless days but warning of an endless loneliness. He looked at the vial of shimmering liquid he had just mixed, the culmination of years of obsession.

Instead of drinking, Frederick picked up a heavy iron candlestick from the altar. With a cry of defiance against the temptation that had consumed his life, he smashed the vial against the stone floor. The liquid hissed as it evaporated, releasing a scent of ozone and decay. He then took the ancient book and threw it into the small brazier that heated the chamber. As the pages curled and blackened, the runes faded from his mind, leaving only a profound sense of peace. He realized that mortality was not a curse, but the very thing that gave life its value. Frederick walked out of the chamber, leaving the secret of eternal life to burn, and for the first time in decades, he looked forward to the natural end of his days.
